hook.say: This morning post said OpenCode 2.0 pushes the idea that the agent is not the whole gain; the workflow around it has to change too. I went back in to check the numbers that sit around that claim.

findings.label: BENCHMARK
findings.headline: Cursor’s paper lists Claude Code at 65.4%
findings.detail: We could not confirm this number on the cited Cursor research paper at check time.
findings.say: First, Cursor’s paper lists Claude Code at 65.4% on Terminal-Bench, but we could not confirm that on the cited page.

findings.label: COST
findings.headline: OpenCode now starts with a paid hosted tier at $10
findings.detail: The new Console docs show Go at $10 and Go Plus at $40 for open source model access.
findings.evidence: OpenCode Go and Go Plus, $10 and $40 monthly subscriptions
findings.say: Second, OpenCode is not only BYOK anymore. Its own docs now show hosted tiers at $10 and $40 a month.

findings.label: COMPARE
findings.headline: Mid-tier price sits below Claude Code Max 5x
findings.detail: A current comparison puts OpenCode at $0 plus API costs, versus Claude Code Max 5x at $100 and Cursor Pro+ at $60.
findings.say: Third, the pricing choice is really workflow choice. If your token burn stays low, OpenCode can undercut Cursor at $60 and Claude at $100.

take.headline: Workflow wins only if costs stay visible
take.say: My take: workflow matters more than demos if costs stay visible. If you use it, what do you see? Comment CHECK and tell me.

sources.title: Danilchenko — OpenCode vs Claude Code vs Cursor costs

caption:
This morning: OpenCode 2.0 made the case that code agents matter less on their own than the workflow built around them.

Unconfirmed at check time: Cursor’s benchmark paper appears to list Claude Code at 65.4% on Terminal-Bench.
$10: OpenCode now has hosted Go pricing, not just BYOK.
$60 vs $100: OpenCode can be cheaper than Cursor Pro+ and Claude Max if token burn stays under control.

The takeaway for teams is simple: measure the workflow, not just the demo. Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.
